messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: INC-47981 fired for service=inference-serving (p99 latency > 1400ms). Alert rule: p99_global > 1400ms for 3m. Autopager: true. route: eng-oncall -> alice_oncall.

alice_oncall: acked. i’m on it — starting quick triage. tagging bob for infra checks.

bob_sre: looking at grafana now. p95 jumped first in apac regions, then us-west. traces show tokenization tasks spiking and a lot of retry loops from the sidecar. seeing increased queue depth on sidecar pools.

charlie_runtime: noted. any recent deploys? I see a deploy of tokenizer-quant patch ~ 30m ago to canary group. pushing a quick diff: reduced batch size + kvcache flags changed.

alice_oncall: can we revert the tokenizer-quant change for canary? if canary is hot, it might be causing cold-cache regressions.

charlie_runtime: rolling back canary now to previous image (svc/tokenizer:2026-03-15-qa -> svc/tokenizer:2026-03-15). running: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/tokenizer tokenizer=repo/tokenizer:stable-20260314`

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-47981 acknowledged by alice_oncall. Escalation policy: default -> will escalate to bob_sre in 5m if not resolved.

maria_support: FYI some customer chats (acct: hyperflow) report slow responses in-prod. I posted their example query in the support thread. looks like responses timeouts on long prompts.

bob_sre: infra note: autoscaler triggered extra workers but they’re coming up slowly due to cold GPU prewarm. sidecar pods are the bottleneck. recommend temporary traffic split to warmed dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-a) and reduce batch_size at ingress.

alice_oncall: agree. charlie, can you change routing policy to prefer dedicated-pool-a for latency-sensitive routes? also drop max_batch_size from 64->32 via feature-flag.

charlie_runtime: applying routing tweak: `redwoodctl route set inference --prefer dedicated-pool-a --selector latency=true` -> applied. Feature-flag change pushed: `FL_MAX_BATCH=32` for front-door sidecars.

bob_sre: doing KV cache warmup job against dedicated-pool-a: `curl -X POST /admin/warm?prefix=tokenizer-default` — kickstarting prefix cache.

alice_oncall: nice. monitoring p95/p99. setting a short-term rate limit for anonymous traffic to reduce noise: `rlimit set global 200rps` (temporary)

incident-bot: update: p99 dropped from ~1.8s to ~1.0s in US-west within 90s of routing change. apac still elevated (~1.4s).

maria_support: keeping customers updated. sending short note: "We observed elevated latency for some requests; engineers have rolled back a recent tokenizer canary and shifted traffic to a warmed pool. Working to fully restore SLAs."

bob_sre: apac nodes still slow because of GPU preemptions and kernel loads. spinning up extra prewarmed instances in apac zone (3 -> 6). ETA ~2m.

charlie_runtime: apac prewarm complete. KV warmers finished. p99 in apac trending down to ~950ms.

alice_oncall: excellent. marking this as mitigated but leaving PD incident open for postmortem. will do a short handoff to oncall rotation and create a follow-up ticket to investigate tokenizer-quant canary behavior + add pre-deploy synthetic warmups.

bob_sre: noted. action items: 1) postmortem + root cause (canary quant flag interaction) 2) add synthetic warmup job to CI for tokenizer changes 3) autoscaler tuning to prefer prewarmed pool for burst 4) improve alert to include canary deploy tags.

charlie_runtime: I'll attach canary diff and logs to the ticket.

alice_oncall: thanks team. tagging @maria_support for customer comms handoff. paging cleared but keeping thread open for 30m for checks. :thumbsup:
